label: calibration of the no-intervention agent simulation to TRA's registered-taxpayer trend

target.series: TRA registered taxpayers, Mainland, NBS Tax Statistics Reports (data/processed/tra_registered_taxpayers.csv)
target.scaling: index anchored to the FinScope 2023 weighted adult TIN rate (3.8281%): target(t) = anchor x registered(t) / registered(2023/24); TRA counts TIN registrations, the agents carry an adult registration rate, so only the GROWTH of the series is matched

method.algorithm: Nelder-Mead (scipy) on the sum of squared differences in percentage points, starts [[-2.0, 0.0], [-3.0, 0.3], [-1.0, -0.2]], 100000 agents, fixed seed (common random numbers)
method.fixed: every other constant of the simulation keeps its current value; the interventions (USSD nudge, urban education) are off; trust and morale are static (Block E3.1: the community-norm feedback and the trust / morale uplift path are retired)

identifiability.reading: a correlation near +-1 or a flat profile means the two parameters are not separately identified by six points; the product conversion x (weighted index + intercept) is what the data pin down

identified_combination.definition: conversion_rate x (mean index of the non-registered agents at the start + intercept): the average yearly registration probability of a non-registered agent before clipping (index = trust, morale, income-rank and mobile-money terms)

searched: FinScope Tanzania 2017 published adult TIN-holding rate: the 2017 questionnaire (FSDT, final 19 April 2017) asks the document question Q27 with code 13 'Tax identification number', the same item as the 2023 variable c27__13, but the published 2017 report 'FinScope Tanzania 2017: Insights that Drive Innovation' (FSDT, 2017) prints no TIN rate: it reports national, voter, TASAF and Zanzibar resident ID (p. 26: 84% of adults hold at least one form of identification) and mobile-money uptake (60% of adults, p. 43). A 2017 level would need the FinScope 2017 microdata, which the project does not hold and which would need a separate data-sharing request to FSDT / NBS.

A TRA or NBS split of registrations into individuals and entities: NBS Tax Statistics Reports 2022/23 and 2023/24 (Table 3.1) give only the total and VAT-registered counts; the TRA Sixth Corporate Plan gives active and dormant BUSINESS TINs for 2020/21, 2021/22 and 2022/23 only (three points, with a definition change in 2022/23, 3.34M to 1.66M); no individual / entity split found.

Yearly NEW registrations (flow): no TRA or NBS publication found with a flow series. A press report of TRA's third-quarter 2025/26 results (900,755 new registrations in nine months; register 8,245,704 at 31 March 2026) exists but is a news item outside the calibration window (2017/18-2023/24), not a TRA document, and is not used.
third_target_search.kept: two parameters (agents.conversion_rate, agents.p_comply.intercept) against the six TRA-index points; the identified combination conversion x (mean index + intercept) is reported in identifiability.identified_combination
